The main methods include: 1. **Brute Force Attack**: This method involves systematically trying all possible combinations of passwords for a known user ID until access is granted. It is generally faster than brute force since it leverages common passwords that users might choose [Source 2]. 3. **Rainbow Table Attack**: This method involves using precomputed tables of hash values for passwords, allowing attackers to quickly look up the hash of a password and find the corresponding plaintext password [Source 2]. 4. **Exploiting Password Policies**: Attackers may also analyze the password policy of a system to determine the complexity and length of passwords that can be used, which can inform their cracking strategy [Source 1].
